question.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(2,1,0)$ and $B(1,3,5).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨1,2,3⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(2,1,0)$ and $B(1,3,5)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨1,3,5⟩-⟨2,1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,2,5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-1,2,5⟩.$ 

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,2,5⟩ & =⟨1,2,3⟩\cdot ⟨-1,2,5⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,2,5⟩ & =18.\end{aligned}
$$
